Run in such a way that you may win it. Athletes exercise self-control in all things. They do not run aimlessly; they run to receive an imperishable reward, not perishable wealth. So I do not run aimlessly, nor do I box as though beating the air, but I punish my body and enslave it, so that after proclaiming to others, I myself should not be disqualified.

It's almost like a pep rally, right? He's telling his workers, "Go out and sell those damn hamburgers, man. I don't care what you do. I don't care how many lies you tell. Go sell those hamburgers. Pretend they're healthy."

Okay? Pretend you love hamburgers. Just pretend. What matters is that you go sell those hamburgers. And guess what, man? Whoever sells those hamburgers gets a car." Okay? But this reward is better than a car because it's the eternal paradise, guys. So go and sell those hamburgers.

When you come together as a church, I hear that there are divisions among you, and to some extent, I believe it. Indeed, there have to be factions among you, for only so will it become clear who among you are genuine. When you come together, it is not really to eat the Lord's supper. For when the time comes to eat, each of you goes ahead with your own supper, and one goes hungry and another becomes drunk.

What do you have at home that you don't share? Or do you show contempt for the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What should I say to you? Should I commend you in this matter? I do not commend you. 

When you come together, it's very important that you obey the ritual. The ritual is communion, the Eucharist. You must remember this is a ritual where you must follow the exact protocols. If you do not, then there's no point in coming to church. So the church is not a place to discuss Jesus or debate Him but to worship Him.

For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you: and the Lord Jesus, on the night when he was betrayed, took a loaf of bread, gave thanks, broke it, and said, "This is my body; do this in remembrance of me." In the same way, after supper, he took the cup, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me."

For as often as you eat the bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until He comes. Whoever therefore eats the bread or drinks the cup in an unworthy manner will be answerable for the body and blood of the Lord. Examine yourselves before eating the bread and drinking from the cup. For all who eat and drink without discerning the body eat and drink judgment against themselves.

For this reason, some are weak and ill, and some have died. But if we judge ourselves, we will not be judged by the Lord. When we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined so that we may not be condemned with the world. So then, when you come together to eat, wait for one another. If you are hungry, eat at home so that when you come together, it will not be for your condemnation.

About other things I will give instruction when I come. 

When Christians partake in the body of Jesus, they believe they are eating His flesh and drinking His blood. They believe this act negates their individuality and makes them one with everyone else. So as you can imagine, what they're doing really is entering into a divine union that transforms them.
